summary: Ensho Kobayashi is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a professorship at Hanazono University (attested in 1988) and later served as professor emeritus there (attested in 2026).
Ensho Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Ryukoku University (attested 1996) under Esho Mikogami. He was a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 2007).

Enshu Kurumiya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Yukio Sakamoto, Ensho Kanakura, and Yosho Nomura, and earned a PhD from the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong (1974), later teaching at Rissho University.

Entai Tomomatsu (1895–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Keio University (~1917–1920) and taught at Taisho University (~1926–1936). He also founded the Publishing Association of Abhidharmakosa-vyakhya.

Erberto Lo Bue (1946–2022) was a scholar of Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD from SOAS University of London (~1976–1981) and held posts at the University of Milan (~1988–1996) and the University of Bologna (~1997–2016).

Eric David Mortensen works in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2003) under Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton, having also studied under Chongren, Xiaoxun, Zhiben, and Xuewen He, and Xi Aniu.

Eric George Hart (1878–1946) was an Indology and linguistics scholar educated at Wellington College and Victoria College, Jersey. From 1926 to 1938, he served as Professor of Arabic, Persian and Hindustani and Reader of Indian History at Trinity College Dublin.

Eric Haruki Swanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held positions at Loyola Marymount University and served as a Senior Visiting Scholar at Stanford University (attested 2026).
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under the supervision of Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe (1933–2000) was a religious studies scholar and Indologist who studied at Manchester and Uppsala under Samuel Brandon and Bengt Sundkler. His posts included Lancaster University, the University of Sydney's first Chair of Religious Studies, and Uppsala University.

Eric M. Greene is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at UC Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf. He has held posts at San Francisco State University (2023) and Yale University, where he became Associate Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2026).

Eric P. Hamp (1920–2019) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Amherst College and Harvard University under Joshua Whatmough. He held academic posts at the University of Michigan (~1950–1953) and the University of Chicago (~1953–1991).

Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by Paul Groner (attested 2012).

Eric Thomas Stokes (1924–1981) was a historian who completed his PhD at Cambridge under Thomas George Percival Spear. He taught at the universities of Malaya, Bristol, and Zimbabwe before serving as Smuts Professor at Cambridge (1970–1981).

Eric Villalobos is an Indology and religious studies doctoral student in Asian, African, and Middle Eastern Religions at Emory University (attested 2026), where he is affiliated with the Graduate Division of Religion.

Erica Baffelli is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied under Massimo Raveri. She held positions at the University of Otago (attested 2015) and the University of Manchester, where she became Professor in Japanese Studies (attested 2026).
Erica Biagetti is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and computational fields. She earned her PhD from the University of Pavia by 2021 and held a post there.

Erich Arno Lehmann (1901–1984) was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Leipzig Evangelical Lutheran Mission and Leipzig University. He held posts at Leipzig, Jena (~1950–1966), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1950–1966) as Dean of Theology.

Erich Berneker (1874–1937) was a linguist who earned his PhD at Leipzig under August Leskien. He taught at Berlin, Prague, Breslau, and the University of Munich, where he was professor of Slavistics from 1911.

Erich Frauwallner (1898–1974) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna under Bernhard Geiger. He spent his career at Vienna as director and professor, and founded the Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Süd- und Ostasiens.
